key_insight: Random vertical placement of perovskite nanowires in AAO pores can improve solar-cell light absorption by combining light trapping and anti-reflection effects.
engineering_relevance: A vertically disordered nanowire architecture may deliver up to 28% higher short-circuit current than ordered arrays while relaxing fabrication constraints on wire length uniformity.
method: Simulated perovskite nanowires embedded at random positions inside AAO membrane pores.
Compared vertically disordered nanowire arrays against corresponding ordered arrays.
Evaluated optical absorption and predicted short-circuit current gains.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to a 28% increase in short-circuit current relative to an ordered perovskite nanowire array.
watch_item: The result is simulation-based, so practical gains will depend on how well the disordered nanowire geometry can be fabricated and integrated reproducibly.
paper_title: Efficient Light Trapping Strategy in Solar Cells via Vertically Disordered Perovskite Nanowires
